title: Do LLM-Judge Biases Compose? Code and data for a label-free, scale-aware test of position-length interaction
description:
Code, judgment data, and analysis pipeline for the manuscript Do LLM-Judge Biases Compose? A Label-Free, Scale-Aware Test for Position–Length Interaction.

Pipelines that use LLMs as pairwise judges correct position and length bias in separate steps, assuming the two add. The manuscript proves that on the win-rate scale any correction applying one position offset across length conditions misstates the verbose-versus-terse contrast by exactly half the position×length interaction, while swap-averaging and stratified correction are exact. It introduces the Swap-Symmetry Interaction Test (SSIT), a design-based difference-in-differences over the four swap cells of each stimulus that needs no labels, and identifies two artefacts that can manufacture the effect: coding ties as votes for a slot, and link curvature near the ceiling. On seven judges from six model families, with swap-equivariant tie coding and inference clustered on 12 distinct stimuli, no judge is individually significant; the pooled interaction is +4.7 win-rate points (95% CI [1.6, 7.8]) and exceeds its curvature baseline.

Contents

  • tmlr/ — manuscript source, PDF, bibliography and figure.
  • analyze_tmlr.py — pilot analysis under three tie codings, stimulus-clustered sign-flip tests, curvature baselines, log-odds interaction and IASC; writes results/tmlr_pilot.json.
  • make_tmlr_figures.py — Figure 1.
  • ssit.py, iasc.py — reference implementations of the test and of Interaction-Aware Swap Correction.
  • sim_ssit_robustness.py, sim_ssit_power.py — simulations behind the manuscript's Tables 1–2.
  • collect_free.py, make_stimulus_pairs.py, make_padded_v.py — judgment collector, stimulus set, and length-only manipulation.
  • data/raw/, data/raw_padded/ — all parsed verdicts from seven judges (gpt-oss-20b/120b, gemma, qwen3-27b, allam-2-7b, mistral-small, command-r) under paraphrase and padding manipulations.
  • Earlier workshop and conference drafts are retained for the record; their per-judge results are superseded (see README).

Dependencies: numpy, scipy, matplotlib (requests for the collector). Seed 2024 throughout.
notes: Accompanies a manuscript prepared for Transactions on Machine Learning Research. An earlier version was a non-archival submission to the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on the Evaluation of LLMs as Judges (JUDGe); its per-judge results are superseded by the corrected analysis in this release.
